events.ai_basis: This approach arose through discussions between the authors and ChatGPT 5.5 and 5.6. / The classification also emerged from discussions between the authors and ChatGPT 5.6, / Building on this classification, the authors directed further discussions with ChatGPT 6 towards the remaining odd part sizes.

events.credibility_reason: Seen only in search snippets, never opened; on the snippet it restates the mozhui-krishna-2025 result, so it is treated as a duplicate rather than a separate advance.

why: Colbrook-Drysdale proves R(G) <= ceil(N/4) for bipartite G and that the crown attains the maximum representation number at every even order, which is the yes/no question as the word-representability literature (Akgun et al.'s conjecture) poses it, so I answered whole. The close call is the reading of 'longest word-representants': if it means minimum length over all, possibly non-uniform, representing words, the paper answers a neighbouring question. I took the representation-number reading because the conjecture this question comes from is stated that way, and I record the alternative in doubts. The paper is an 18-day-old preprint with no human reading, so it is unreviewed; the Lean build and SAT certificates do not count as digestion (F7). Nothing specific counts against it, so it is credible. On AI: the authors' own declaration says the approach behind the principal advance, the obstruction classification and the odd-part argument came out of discussions with ChatGPT 5.5/5.6/6. Those are parts of the proof's mathematics inside human-led work, so the role is assisted, not generated. The Codex entries (counting, certificates, Lean) add nothing beyond that. Mozhui-Krishna 2025 settles every bipartite class except equal even parts, so it is a case. The thesis duplicates it and is snippet-only, so I scored it none. Hefty et al. has only a year-only 2024 date and no shown bearing on the question. The pre-snapshot papers only pose the conjecture or give the crown's value (none), apart from a general upper bound (bound).
doubts: The word-length reading is unresolved. Under the minimum-length-over-all-words reading (Gaetz-Ji ell(G)), crown extremality is not shown unless minimum-length representants are uniform. On that reading the 2026 event would be a variant. The AI declaration quotes came from a summarising fetch, not raw text. The ScienceDirect 2026 'Bottlenecks and bounds' paper was never opened and may bear on the question.
